title: Calibrate T4 Thresholds and Guards
objective: Review audit data from P27-T1 through P27-T4 and adjust T4 activation thresholds and guard conditions if needed to ensure stable negative relational continuity, or explicitly confirm current parameters are sufficient.
exact_scope: IN: Review audit metrics from P27 instrumentation (composition collision rates, activation frequency, downstream propagation depth, _adjust_t4() stability data); adjust threshold constants and guard logic in T4 builder and _adjust_t4() if audit reveals calibration needs; add narrow protective filters if same-day composition risks or wake chain anomalies detected; document calibration decisions. OUT: Changes to settlement substrate, bridge architecture modifications, new event taxonomy, player-side intervention systems, LLM integration, removal of existing audit instrumentation, broad relational system redesign.
constraints: Must preserve all existing audit instrumentation from P27-T1 through P27-T4
Must not break existing 296+ test assertions
Changes must be justified by specific audit data findings
If no calibration changes are needed, must explicitly document this conclusion with rationale
Must maintain narrow T4 activation seam approved in Phase 26B
acceptance_criteria: T4 activation thresholds are either adjusted based on audit data or explicitly confirmed sufficient with documented rationale
Guard conditions either modified to address identified risks or explicitly confirmed adequate
All existing tests continue to pass without regression
Calibration changes do not increase T2/T4 same-day composition collision rates beyond observed baseline
Downstream wake chain depth remains within acceptable bounds after any threshold adjustments
required_tests: test that T4 activation frequency remains within expected bounds after threshold calibration
test that same-day T2/T4 composition safety is preserved under calibrated parameters
test that downstream residual creation stability is maintained after guard adjustments
non_goals: do not refactor unrelated bridge or settlement code
do not add new major event types or social event taxonomy
do not implement LLM appraisal or live runtime features
do not remove or disable existing audit instrumentation
